newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro's power industry worth $1.12 bln.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro's power industry worth $1.12 bln.

text.p: Economists said on Thursday the electric power industry in the Yugoslav republic of Montenegro is worth $1.12 billion.
"The government has accepted our evaluation of the electric power industry of $1.12 billion," Petar Ivanovic of the Podgorica economic faculty told Reuters by telephone.
The figure includes the value of two hydro-electric plants and one thermal power plant, a system of seven small hydro-electric power stations and the entire transmission and distribution system.
Ivanovic said the estimate was the first part of a comprehensive study for the eventual privatisation of Montenegro's electric power industry.
The $1.12 billion would be used as a base figure for the industry's privatisation, he said. "But it is also an initial report for potential foreign investors."
The privatisation study is expected to be finished by the end of next year, he said.
Ivanovic, who was number two in the team of more than a hundred researchers, said the study treated electricity as a commodity.
The value represented the lion's share of those companies in Montenegro which have amended their legal status from "socially-owned" to state-run firms, he added.
Montenegrin authorities say clearly defining ownership in state industries is the first step towards privatisation.
The Yugoslav republic of Serbia has commissioned a study of the value of the country's Postal Telephone and Telegraph company, according to local media.
After four years of war, Yugoslavia is comprised of Serbia and the tiny republic of Montenegro. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom 381 11 222 4254
